name: ad
title: Ad
summary: A 6, 15 or 30-second ad in 16:9, 1:1 or 9:16: one message, the brand, and at most one call to action.
use_when: Paid placement: pre-roll, in-feed or a vertical ad slot. Pick the length first; the structure follows from it.

pace.note: Short-film placement; a 6-second ad often has no voice at all.

beats.name: message
beats.job: One message and the brand. Nothing else fits in six seconds.

beats.name: hook
beats.job: The reason to keep watching, in the first two seconds.

beats.name: proof
beats.job: One sourced fact or the product working.

beats.name: call to action
beats.job: One action and where to take it; the brand on screen as it lands.

rules: The brand shows early and again at the end.
It reads with the sound off: captions and supers carry the words.
One call to action, never two.

captions.position: inside the channel's safe zone for the aspect
captions.note: Square and vertical cuts use shorter lines (36 and 32 characters).

budget.note: Generation only when it's allowed and adds something.

notes: For a TV or cinema spot, set broadcast: true in film.json: loudness moves to EBU R 128 or ATSC A/85, and the score needs an Eleven Music Enterprise licence.
Each aspect is its own derived film with its own layout: a 9:16 ad is re-staged, never a crop of the 16:9 one.
The end hold is 1.5 s (qa's end_hold): a six-second ad is one message and the brand, so the films' 3 s end card would be half of it; the call to action holds still for its last 1.5 s at every length.
